baseline_report: Severe hypertension (221/85 mm Hg) with renal insufficiency, markedly elevated BNP (838.6 pg/mL), and echocardiographic left atrial enlargement with mild pulmonary hypertension indicate cardiac target-organ damage, establishing hypertensive emergency. Atrial flutter is best explained as secondary to hypertensive heart disease, not a primary arrhythmia; absence of troponin elevation and ischemic ECG changes reduces acute coronary syndrome, and bradyarrhythmia is refuted by the overall picture. Thus the frontier is sufficiently refined to conclude hypertensive emergency complicated by acute heart failure.
